subject: Prepay true-up mechanics & ramp schedule — Quantix multi-year proposal
messages:
From: Ari Levin <ari@quantix.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sasha Park <sasha.park@quantix.ai>, procurement@quantix.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on prepay true-up + ramp for multi-year commit

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quantix is interested in a 3-year prepay but we have a few questions before we proceed to legal/procurement:

- True-up cadence: do you do annual true-ups only or a final end-of-term reconciliation (or both)?
- Buffer bands: what tolerance do you typically allow before invoicing overage (e.g., +/-10%)?
- Overage calc: is overage invoiced at a per-token list rate, or a blended rate based on committed pricing?
- Ramp: can we front-load year 1 and have a defined ramp schedule year 2/3 without losing the multi-year discount?

Attached is our RFP and expected ramp: Year 1 = 60% commitment, Year 2 = 90%, Year 3 = 120% (of baseline annual units). Were also asking for the economic impact if consumption overshoots by 10-30% in any year.

Can you share a short note on how Redwood structures true-ups and whether theres room to cap overage charges or apply refunds/credits at end of term?

Appreciate a quick note so procurement can decide next steps.

Best,
Ari

Attachment: Quantix_RFP_v2.pdf (summary deck)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ari Levin <ari@quantix.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on prepay true-up + ramp for multi-year commit

Ari,

Thanks for the clear ramp schedule — that helps. High level response below; we can produce a short term sheet once you confirm the approach you prefer.

1) Cadence: Redwood supports an annual true-up (30 days after each 12-mo anniversary) plus a final EOT (end-of-term) reconciliation within 90 days of the final term. The annual true-ups settle obvious mismatches promptly; the EOT true-up is the single-source reconciliation for refunds/long-tail credits.

2) Buffer bands: for multi-year prepay we typically allow a forgiveness band to avoid noisy micro-billing. Proposal for Quantix: +/-15% buffer in Year 1 (to accommodate initial variability), then +/-10% for Years 2 & 3. Bands are applied to committed units per year.

3) Overage calculation: if consumption in a given year > committed units + buffer, overage is invoiced at an overage rate equal to the LOWER of (a) Redwood list overage rate, or (b) 1.25x the committed unit price for the relevant year (this caps runaway charges). At EOT reconciliation, overages and under-consumption are netted.

4) Credits / refunds: under-consumption is first applied as credits against future invoices. If there is no renewal within 60 days after EOT reconciliation, residual credits are refunded pro-rata at the committed unit price (not the discounted list price).

5) Ramp and discounts: we can accommodate your ramp (60/90/120) and protect the multi-year discount schedule provided you keep a minimum aggregate prepay threshold across the 3 years. Proposed term discounts: 7% for annual prepay (single year), or a stepped 3-year profile of 10% / 12% / 15% year-over-year for an executed 3-year prepay. The effective committed unit price for each year is the list unit price less that year's discount.

Ive attached a draft term sheet that includes the clause language for true-up and overages. If that structure looks good, Ill loop in Finance and Legal to finalize language and produce a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — want to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk through one worked example (e.g., year 2 at +25% consumption)?

- Marissa

Attachment: Draft_SOW_and_TermSheet.pdf
From: Sasha Park <sasha.park@quantix.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Ari Levin <ari@quantix.ai>, procurement@quantix.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on prepay true-up + ramp for multi-year commit

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifying items from procurement:

- Overage basis: does "committed unit price" mean per-embedding/token or per-request product SKU? We need explicit mapping because our billing model is a combination of embeddings and generation tokens.
- Blended calc: please show a worked example for Year 2 where committed unit price = $0.006/token, list overage = $0.009/token, consumption = 125% of committed after buffer. How is the overage invoice computed?
- Overage cap: Quantix asks that overage charge be capped to 125% of the committed unit price (we like that the cap aligns to your 1.25x suggestion) — can you confirm you will include that in the term sheet?
- Annual vs EOT: procurement prefers annual reconciliation only (no separate EOT true-up). Would Redwood accept annual-only true-ups if we agree to a small holdback (2% of prepay) to be reconciled at contract termination?

If you can provide a one-page worked example and confirm the cap language, procurement is ready to circulate to legal.

Best,
Sasha
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed true-up/overage contract language (draft)

Folks,

Below is suggested contract language we can drop into the term sheet to address procurements asks. This is internal draft; feel free to comment.

"True-Up and Overage Reconciliation":
- Annual reconciliation: Customer and Redwood will reconcile actual consumption against committed units within 30 days following each 12-month anniversary ("Annual True-Up"). Parties may also elect a single End-of-Term reconciliation within 90 days of final term; however, Annual True-Ups will be treated as the primary settlement mechanism.
- Buffer Band: For the first contract year, a tolerance band of +/-15% will apply to the committed units. For each subsequent contract year, a tolerance band of +/-10% will apply. Overages will be calculated on units exceeding (Committed Units + Buffer Band).
- Overage Rate and Cap: Overage units will be invoiced at the lesser of (i) the published Redwood list overage rate, or (ii) 1.25x the applicable committed unit price. Redwood will not invoice at a rate higher than 125% of the committed unit price for any overage.
- Credits/Refunds: Under-consumption (units below committed) will be applied as credits to future invoices. If no renewal is executed within 60 days following the final reconciliation, remaining credits will be refunded at the committed unit price on a pro rata basis.
- Audit Rights: Customer may request, no more than once annually, reasonable access to consumption logs for verification purposes; Redwood will provide redacted logs sufficient to validate units consumed.

Im comfortable with the cap language requested by procurement; it aligns with our risk posture and keeps a predictable worst-case exposure for customers. If procurement wants to remove EOT reconciliation entirely in exchange for a 2% holdback, we can accept that commercially but would like the holdback applied to the final annual invoice to preserve cashflow predictability.

If approved, Ill prepare the legal language for the term sheet and instruct Sales Ops to generate a DocuSign envelope.

- Lauren
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ari Levin <ari@quantix.ai>, Sasha Park <sasha.park@quantix.ai>, procurement@quantix.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on prepay true-up + ramp for multi-year commit — next steps

Ari/Sasha,

Thanks for the quick back-and-forth. To confirm the working approach that Legal and Finance are ready to put into the term sheet:

- Annual true-ups (30 days post-anniversary) as primary settlement; optional EOT reconciliation within 90 days but not required if you prefer annual-only with a 2% holdback.
- Buffer bands: +/\u221215% Year 1, +/\u221210% Years 2-3.
- Overage invoiced at the lower of list overage rate or 1.25x committed unit price (this provides the 125% cap you requested).
- Credits applied to future invoices; refunds only if no renewal within 60 days after final reconciliation.

If that aligns with Quantix internal approval, please confirm in reply and well circulate the final term sheet + DocuSign (HubSpot deal attached). If you prefer annual-only (no EOT) with the 2% holdback, note that in your reply and well reflect that change.

Assuming approval, next steps: Sales Ops will prepare a term sheet and DocuSign envelope; Legal will include the audit language above; Finance will model the expected revenue recognition and apply the stepped discount schedule (10/12/15).

Would you like a 30-minute call Friday to walk through the worked example and the draft term sheet?

Cheers,
Marissa
